packaging.title: feat(specifiers): add `__replace__` to Specifier and SpecifierSet
packaging.body:
This API provides a direct alternative to `Specifier` and `SpecifierSet` mutable prerelease, which I would like to deprecate.

However, upon down a survey of downstream projects, I found many that currently use the mutability of packaging's specifiers. So I will not deprecate until at least the next release after `__replace__` is added. I will also open  PRs on those projects and add some of them to packaging's downstream tests.

ripgrep.title: ignore: respect linked worktree excludes without requiring Git
ripgrep.body:
## Summary

With `require_git(false)`, the `ignore` crate does not apply the common Git directory's `info/exclude` rules when traversing a linked worktree. It skips probing the worktree's `.git` file, so it cannot resolve the shared repository directory that owns those excludes.

Probe `.git` whenever Git excludes are enabled, even when repository detection is not required. The existing linked-worktree resolution then finds the shared `info/exclude` file. Extend the existing linked-worktree regression to cover `require_git(false)`.

## Verification

Verified against `ignore` 0.4.33.

- [x] The added `require_git(false)` assertion fails before the fix.
- [x] The existing linked-worktree test passes with the fix, including the new assertion.

```sh
cargo nextest run -p ignore --lib -E 'test(git_info_exclude_in_linked_worktree)'
```

The focused test failed before the fix and passed afterward (one test, 0.003 seconds).

jq.title: Fix halt_error adding a newline to non-string output
jq.body:
Fixes #3693.

`halt_error` prints string inputs with `priv_fwrite` (no newline), but the non-string branch used `fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", ...)`, adding a newline that the manual explicitly rules out:

```console
$ jq -n '{"a":"xyz"}|halt_error(1)' 2>&1 | wc -c
12    # before
11    # after
```

The fix uses the same `priv_fwrite` call as the string branch:

```c
error_message = jv_dump_string(error_message, 0);
priv_fwrite(jv_string_value(error_message),
    jv_string_length_bytes(jv_copy(error_message)),
    stderr, dumpopts & JV_PRINT_ISATTY);
```

## Tests

Added a byte-count assertion to `tests/shtest`. The existing check used command substitution, which strips trailing newlines, so it could not detect this.

- red: `12` bytes, `make check` fails
- green: `11` bytes, `make check` passes (`FAIL: 0`)

marked.title: fix: apply emphasis flanking and rules 9-10 to the whole delimiter run
marked.body: **Marked version:** 18.1.1 (master at 6dd5b3c) **Markdown flavor:** CommonMark (GitHub Flavored Markdown output is the same for these inputs) ## Description No existing issue. Below is the issue in the template's format. ## Expectation Emphasis should follow CommonMark 0.31.2 (6.2, rules 9 and 10). Flanking and the "multiple of 3" rule look at the whole delimiter run that holds the opener. The rule also applies when the opener can close as well as open, not only when the closer can open. Expected output is what commonmark.js 0.31.2 gives: | input | commonmark.js | marked 18.1.1 | |---|---|---| | `***.a*` | `**.a` | `***.a*` | | `**(a)*` | `*(a)` | `**(a)*` | | `foo ***!bar*` | `foo **!bar` | `foo ***!bar*` | | `a*b**` | `a*b**` | `ab*` | | `x a*b** y` | `x a*b** y` | `x ab* y` | | `__(_*` | `__(_*` | `_(*` | ## Result There are two causes, both in `emStrong`. 1. When the whole run can't close, the lexer takes its first delimiter as text and tries the rest again. On that retry `prevChar` is the delimiter itself (`*`). The `punctuation` rule leaves out `*` and `_`, so if the run is followed by punctuation (`**(a)*`) the left-flanking check fails, and the shorter opener never gets tried. For `_` the retry keeps the right `prevChar`, but rules 9-10 then count only what is left of the run (`__(_*` gives 1 + 1 rather than 2 + 1). 2. Rules 9-10 were only applied when the closer could open (`match[5]`/`match[6]`), never when the opener could close. In `a*b**` the `*` is both left- and right-flanking, so 1 + 2 is a multiple of 3 and it must not pair with `**`. ## What was attempted `emStrong` now walks back through `maskedSrc` to the start of the current run. Masking keeps the length, and escaped delimiters are masked as `+`, so a run of delimiter characters there is the real run. The character before the run is used for the flanking check on a mid-run retry. The full run length is used for rules 9-10. That same character tells us whether the opener can also close; when it can, rules 9-10 apply to closers that can only close too. The other delimiter character (`_` before `**`) counts as punctuation for that check, as it does in CommonMark. Pedantic mode is not changed, since markdown.pl has none of these rules. The existing mid-run guard from #4008 (`**a*b*c`) is kept and now runs before the rule 9-10 check. ## Contributor - [x] Test(s) exist to ensure functionality and minimize regression (if no tests added, list tests covering this PR); or, - [ ] no tests required for this PR. - [ ] If submitting new feature, it has been documented in the appropriate places. Added `test/specs/new/em_strong_delimiter_run.{md,html}`. The expected HTML was generated with commonmark.js 0.31.2, and marked's output matches it with `gfm` on and off. It also includes `a_*a_**`, which already passed, to cover the `_`-before-`*` punctuation case. What was run: - `npm test` (build:reset, build:docs, test:specs, test:unit, test:umd, test:cjs, test:types, test:lint): passes. Specs: 1913 pass, 0 fail. Unit: 199 pass. - The new fixture fails without the `src/Tokenizer.ts` change and passes with it. - Differential check against commonmark.js 0.31.2 on 100k random strings built from `*`, `_`, letters, spaces, `.`, `(`, `)` and `ö` (`gfm: false`): divergences go from 167 to 66 (103 fixed). Two inputs now diverge that matched before, `__****(**__` and `__ __****_ö**__`. Both are `****(**` nested inside `__…__`. That inner text is lexed again on its own, so it loses the outer context. Before, the inner text was wrong on its own (`****(**` stayed literal), and that happened to hide the problem. Similar runs with GFM on, and with block markup and reference links in the mix, showed fixes and no new divergences. - Pedantic output, before against after, on 50k random emphasis strings: identical. - Rough timing on README, docs, `test/specs/new`, `test/specs/original` and the CommonMark examples, 20 passes each: no difference beyond noise. Very long runs of a single delimiter (20,000 `*`) were already quadratic and are about 20% slower. A 20,000-`*` run followed by punctuation, which used to fail fast and now searches for a closer, went from about 0.76 s to 3.7 s. If that's not acceptable I can look for a way to keep the fast path. This also touches the same code as #4103, so one of the two will need a rebase. Not run: `npm run test:redos` (no regex was changed), browser tests, `npm run bench`. Out of scope: inputs like `***ab**b` (expected `*abb`) still differ. They need the mid-run opener to pair with a closer that can also open, and the #4008 guard prevents that. Mixed `*`/`_` nesting cases also remain. ## Committer In most cases, this should be a different person than the contributor. - [ ] CI is green (no forced merge required). - [ ] Squash and Merge PR following [conventional commit guidelines](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/).

go-git.title: plumbing: object, Decode tree entry modes as Git does
go-git.body:
go-git reads the mode of a tree entry differently from Git in two ways. As a result, a tree Git reads without issue either fails to decode or decodes with a different mode:

1. `filemode.FromBytes` rejects a mode longer than 7 digits, while Git's `parse_mode` accepts any nonempty run of octal digits ([object.h#L200-L215](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.55.0/object.h#L200-L215)). Git accepts a zero-padded mode such as `00000000000100644` when reading a tree (`git ls-tree` prints `100644`), but go-git fails with `malformed tree: malformed mode`. A mode longer than the 4096-byte read buffer of `Tree.Decode` fails with a bare `bufio.ErrBufferFull` instead of `ErrMalformedTree`.
2. When canonicalising a regular file, go-git tests any of the execute bits (`0o111`). Git's `canon_mode` only looks at the owner execute bit (`0o100`, see [object.h#L133-L154](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.55.0/object.h#L133-L154)). Due to this, go-git reads a stored `100011` as `100755` where Git reads `100644`.

The following reproduces both:

```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/object"
)

func main() {
	hash := bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xAA}, 20)
	for _, mode := range []string{"00000000000100644", "100011"} {
		obj := &plumbing.MemoryObject{}
		obj.SetType(plumbing.TreeObject)
		_, _ = obj.Write(append([]byte(mode+" a\x00"), hash...))

		var tree object.Tree
		if err := tree.Decode(obj); err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("%s: %v\n", mode, err)
			continue
		}
		fmt.Printf("%s: %s\n", mode, tree.Entries[0].Mode)
	}
}
```

On `main` this prints:

```
00000000000100644: malformed tree: malformed mode
100011: 0100755
```

With this change, the example prints `0100644` for both entries. This is the same mode that `git ls-tree` reports as `100644` for equivalent raw tree entries written using `git hash-object --literally -t tree`.

This PR is split into two commits:

1. `Tree.Decode` now reads a mode of any length and keeps the low 32 bits of a wider value. Git keeps the low 16 bits, but `canon_mode` only reads bits both keep, so the canonical result is the same. A mode that does not fit in its buffer is read in chunks, in constant memory, and every malformed mode is reported as `ErrMalformedTree`. `filemode.FromBytes` accepts input longer than 7 digits as well, but still returns an error for a value wider than 32 bits, like `filemode.New`.
2. A new `filemode.FileMode.Canonical` maps a stored mode to the mode Git acts on, as `canon_mode` does, and `Tree.Decode` now uses it instead of its private `canonicalTreeMode`.

The second commit changes behaviour for regular-file entries whose group or other execute bits are set while the owner execute bit is clear. These now decode as `100644`, so merges and commits built from such a tree record `100644`, and checkout writes the file without execute permission. Existing commits do not change. A worktree an earlier go-git checked out from such a tree shows the file as modified in `Status` until it is reset, which is also what Git reports for it.

Besides unit tests for `FromBytes` and `Canonical`, `TestTreeDecodeModesMatchGit` writes trees with unusual modes (zero-padded, over 4096 digits, `100011`, `100664`, `120777`, `160777`, `0`, and others) using `git hash-object --literally`, and checks that `Tree.Decode` returns the mode `git ls-tree` prints for each. The test is skipped when `git` is unavailable or when tests run with `-short`. `FuzzTreeDecode` now also asserts that every decoded mode is canonical.

black.title: Fix crash on `# fmt: skip` on a nested bracket after `with` or `yield`
black.body:
### Description

`# fmt: skip` on an opening bracket crashes Black when the bracket starts an operand that's nested inside a longer expression after `with` or `yield`:

```python
with (  # fmt: skip
    a
) == 1 and b:
    pass
```

fails with "INTERNAL ERROR: Black produced invalid code: cannot parse: 1:4". The same happens with `) + 1 == 2:`, `with not (  # fmt: skip` ... `) or b:`, `async with`, and `with ... as c`. After `yield` the output still parses but means something else (`yield` ends up on its own line), so Black reports "produced code that is not equivalent to the source". 26.10.1 crashes on these too.

To find the code before the bracket on the same line, the walk in `_generate_ignored_nodes_from_fmt_skip` climbs to the parent when a node has no previous sibling, but only by one level. Here the bracket is the first leaf of a `comparison` inside an `and_test`, so the walk stops at the `comparison` and `with` is never added to the skipped line. The skipped code then becomes a standalone comment after `with`, which gets split onto its own line.

Both climbs (the one before the walk and the one inside it) now keep going up while the node is the first child of its parent. The inner loop that collapsed fully ignored parents is folded into the outer one, since it did the same climb with an extra condition.

With the whole line skipped, a unary operator before the bracket can be hidden while its operand goes on after the closing bracket (`with -(  # fmt: skip` ... `).y and b:`). That leaves a `factor` node with only the operand, so `visit_factor` now checks the number of children instead of unpacking two.

In other statements this didn't crash, but the line wasn't kept as is either. For example `x = (  # fmt: skip` ... `) == 1 and b` was turned into `x = (` followed by the bracket on its own line. Those lines are now left unchanged. Code that was already formatted by Black stays the same: I ran ~19k generated variants (`x =`, `return`, `yield`, `with`, `if`, `assert`, lambdas, unary operators, trailers, and/or/comparison/arithmetic operands) and the output of `main` for each one is unchanged with this branch, in stable, preview and unstable. None of them crash now.

### Checklist - did you ...

- [x] Implement any code style changes under the `--preview` style, following the stability policy?
- [x] Add an entry in `CHANGES.md` if necessary?
- [x] Add / update tests if necessary?
- [x] Add new / update outdated documentation?

sympy.title: geometry: direct symbolic formulas for Plane.distance
sympy.body:
<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
* geometry
  * Updated `Plane.distance` to use direct closed-form symbolic formulas for `Point3D`, `LinearEntity3D` (`Segment3D`, `Ray3D`, `Line3D`), and `Plane`, enabling exact evaluation on symbolic coordinates without `Undecidable` errors.
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->

#### References to other Issues or PRs
Fixes #30790

#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed
Previously, `Plane.distance(o)` used intersection checks (`self.intersection(o)` and `pi in o`), which fail on symbolic coordinates with `Undecidable: Cannot determine if ... is in ...` (e.g. `p.distance(Segment3D(Point3D(0, 0, z1), Point3D(0, 0, z2)))`).

Following the Lean4-backed closed-form formulas proposed by @sylee957 in #30778 (comment 6302265516), this PR updates `Plane.distance` to use direct closed-form formulas:
- **`Point3D`**: `Abs(a) / N`
- **`Segment3D`**: `(Abs(a) + Abs(b) - Abs(c)) / (2 * N)`
- **`Ray3D`**: `Abs(a) * (1 + Min(0, sign(a * c))) / N`
- **`Line3D`**: `Abs(a) * (1 - Abs(sign(c))) / N`
- **`Plane`**: `self.distance(o.p1)` if `self.is_parallel(o)` else `S.Zero`

Where $P = \text{self.p1}$, $n = \text{Point3D(self.normal\_vector)}$, $a = n \cdot (A - P)$, $b = n \cdot (B - P)$, $c = n \cdot (B - A)$, and $N = \sqrt{n \cdot n}$.

#### Other comments
All existing tests in `sympy/geometry/tests/test_plane.py` continue to pass. A comprehensive regression test suite `test_plane_distance_symbolic` has been added covering symbolic segments, rays, lines, and point conversions.

#### AI Generation Disclosure
I have read the SymPy instructions on using AI tools and I certify that I have:
- Verified all mathematical formulas and edge cases (segments crossing planes, rays directed towards/away/parallel, lines intersecting/parallel, in-plane entities, and arbitrary symbolic coordinate inputs).
- Tested the code thoroughly against the entire `sympy.geometry.plane` test suite and added comprehensive regression tests.

pytest.title: feat(mark): expose `pytest.ParameterSet` in public API (#13431)
pytest.body:
### Description

This PR addresses #13431 (part of the public API typing roadmap #7469) by exposing `ParameterSet` in the public `pytest` namespace as the return type of `pytest.param()`.

Currently, developers using `pytest.param` in typed helper functions that return parameter sets receive private import warnings (such as Pyright's `reportPrivateImportUsage`) when importing `ParameterSet` from `_pytest.mark.structures`.

### Summary of Changes

- **Public export**: Exposed `pytest.ParameterSet` in `src/pytest/__init__.py` and included it in `__all__`.
- **Module declaration**: Set `__module__ = "pytest"` on `ParameterSet`.
- **Private constructor**: Refactored `ParameterSet` as a `NamedTuple` subclass with a `__new__` constructor that calls `check_ispytest(_ispytest)` so direct instantiation issues a `PytestDeprecationWarning`, while internal factories (`pytest.param()`, `extract_from()`, etc.) instantiate with `_ispytest=True`.
- **Factory methods**: Marked internal classmethods (`param`, `extract_from`) with `:meta private:` so Sphinx autodoc does not surface them under `pytest.ParameterSet`.
- **Documentation**: Added `pytest.ParameterSet` to `doc/en/reference/reference.rst` under `Objects`, and removed the obsolete entry from `nitpick_ignore` in `doc/en/conf.py`.
- **Changelog**: Added `changelog/13431.improvement.rst`.
- **Tests**: Added comprehensive unit tests in `testing/test_mark.py` verifying public export, `isinstance` checking, deprecation warning on unflagged initialization, and `pickle` serialization.
- **Authors**: Added myself to `AUTHORS`.

Closes #13431.

commander.body:
## Problem

A global option value with an unknown source fails to mask the leaf option value source in `.getOptionValueSourceWithGlobals()`

prometheus.title: api/prometheus: escape label names containing '/' in LabelValues
prometheus.body:
`LabelValues` puts the label name into the request path, `/api/v1/label/<name>/values`. With UTF-8 label names, a name like `app.kubernetes.io/name` adds extra path segments, the request doesn't match the route any more, and Prometheus answers 404.

The Prometheus HTTP API docs say a name containing `/` has to be sent in the Values Escaping form, `U__app_2e_kubernetes_2e_io_2f_name`, and the server decodes that form since v3.0.1 (prometheus/prometheus 12577e385). This change escapes the name that way when it contains a `/`, or when it is exactly `.` or `..`, because Prometheus serves the API behind `http.ServeMux`, which cleans those segments out of the path and answers 404. Every other name, including dotted ones like `service.name`, is sent exactly as before, so requests that work today don't change.

How I checked it:

Table cases in `TestAPIs` for `service.name` (unchanged path), `app.kubernetes.io/name`, `.` and `..` (escaped paths). The second one fails on main with `got /api/v1/label/app.kubernetes.io/name/values`.

An end-to-end check with the real `api.NewClient` against an httptest server using `prometheus/common/route` with the same `label/:name/values` route and `U__` decoding as Prometheus: on main the call returns `client error: 404`, with the change it returns the label.

@bwplotka @kakkoyun

fd.title: Fix integer overflow when parsing size constraints with large values.
fd.body:
Previously, multiplying the parsed quantity by its unit multiplier in the size module could overflow u64, causing a panic in debug builds or producing an incorrect value in typical release builds. This PR replaces direct multiplication with checked_mul() so that overflowing values are rejected as invalid size constraints.

Changes
* Replace direct multiplication with checked_mul() in size filter parsing.
* Add regression tests for overflowing values across different units and filter types.
* Add a test to verify that u64::MAX bytes is still accepted.

fmt.title: Fix signs in floating-point duration formatting
fmt.body:
Negative floating durations repeat the minus sign with multiple chrono conversions, while negative infinity loses it. Reuse write_sign() in both paths to emit one leading minus, preserving precision, padding and positive/NaN behavior.

Both regression tests fail before the fix. All 22 test executables pass with GCC C++11, Clang C++20 and Windows MSVC C++20. Header-only probes, source formatting and diff checks pass. Windows uses the default warning policy; enabling WERROR additionally hits an unchanged GCC pragma.

cli11.title: fix: parse complex numbers with an exponent in the imaginary part
cli11.body:
A `std::complex` option given a single string fails to convert when the imaginary part has an exponent, e.g. `-c 1+2e-3i`, `-c 1.5e-1-2.5e-1i` or `-c 2e-3i` ("Could not convert: -c = 1+2e-3i"). Exponents already work for `double` options and in the real part (`1e-3+2i`).

The complex `lexical_cast` split the string at the last `+`/`-`, which in these inputs is the exponent's sign, so the real part became `1+2e` and the conversion failed. It now tries the signs from the right and splits at the last one where both the real and the imaginary part convert. If no split works, the input is parsed as a single real or imaginary number, as before, and then falls back to the stream conversion. Choosing the split by whether both halves convert, rather than by "sign after `e`", keeps hex input such as `0x1e+2i` working.

Validation:
- New `ComplexSingleArgExponentOption` test in `tests/NewParseTest.cpp` covers `1+2e-3i`, `1.5e-1-2.5e-1i`, `-1e-2-3e-2j`, `1.5E+2-3E+1j`, `2e-3i`, `1e-5` (still real only) and checks that `1+2e-3+4i` is still rejected. It fails on current `main` with `Could not convert: --complex = 1+2e-3i` and passes with the change.
- The existing complex tests (`ComplexSingleArgOption`, `ComplexSingleImagOption`, `LexicalCastParsable`, ...) are unchanged and pass.
- Default header-only build with warnings as errors (GCC 13, C++17): 82/82 CTest targets pass. C++11 build: 24/24 pass.
- clang-format 23.1.2, cpplint, codespell and clang-tidy (tidy preset settings) are clean on the changed files.

commons-lang.title: Add optional FIFO fairness to TimedSemaphore (LANG-1790)
commons-lang.body:
Add optional FIFO fairness to TimedSemaphore (LANG-1790).

Offered as an alternative to PR #1544 

This changeset addresses LANG-1790 while preserving the existing default behavior and public API.

The main difference is that fairness is enforced by an explicit FIFO queue. In the original PR, callers still block on `Object.wait()`, while the backing `Semaphore` is only polled with immediate acquisition attempts. Those callers never join the semaphore’s waiting queue, so its fairness setting cannot enforce their acquisition order.

This implementation also:

- Keeps permit acquisition, accounting, limit changes, and period rollover under the same monitor, avoiding the race between consuming a permit and updating `acquireCount`.
- Preserves the non-throwing `tryAcquire()` signature and documents that it can bypass queued callers.
- Handles interruption and shutdown by removing the correct queue entry and notifying remaining callers.
- Preserves unlimited-mode behavior: new acquisitions proceed immediately, and existing waiters can proceed at rollover.
- Documents the actual ordering guarantee without referring to a timed `tryAcquire()` overload that this class does not provide.

The regression tests establish that callers are waiting before checking ordering. They cover newcomer bypass prevention, explicit non-fair behavior, cancellation, shutdown, limit changes, and builder reuse. A controlled test also distinguishes FIFO behavior from non-fair behavior without relying on thread-start order or unrestricted completion order.

The original enhancement request is valid; these changes make the fairness guarantee effective while avoiding compatibility and concurrency regressions.

libarchive.title: read_data_into_fd: Fix spurious "Seek error" when appending to a non-empty file
libarchive.body:
Since 3.8.8, extracting into a non-empty file opened for appending fails, although the data is written:

```
$ echo header > out
$ bsdtar -xOf t.tar f >> out
f: Seek error: Unknown error -1
bsdtar: Error exit delayed from previous errors
$ echo $?
1
```

`bsdcat f.gz >> out` fails the same way, and `bsdtar -xO` stops after the first entry.
The final check from #3128 compares how far the descriptor offset moved with the bytes written, but with O_APPEND the first write moves the offset to the end of the file.

Following stoeckmann's suggestion, archive_read_data_into_fd() no longer seeks over holes when the descriptor is not a regular file or was opened with O_APPEND. Holes are written as zeros, so the check holds and sparse entries append correctly too.

test_read_data_into_fd_append appends two plain entries and a sparse one to a non-empty file. It fails without the fix with "Seek error" and passes with it. On Windows it runs with its own expected output, because WriteFile() ignores the CRT's O_APPEND. The suite passes in an ASan and UBSan build.

expat.title: lib: Take CDATA sections, comments and PI into account with entity scanning (follow-up to #1433, fixes #1438)

rspec.title: Apply config.extend modules before config.include modules
rspec.body:
`Configuration#configure_group` applies `config.include` modules before `config.extend` modules. `config.include_context` registers the shared context as an include module, and its `included` hook evaluates the shared context block right away, before the group has been extended. Calling a method from a `config.extend` module inside a shared context added with `config.include_context` raises `NameError`.

Apply extend modules first so their methods are available when the shared context block is evaluated.

Fixes #34
